title: Asia 7 of 7 · Southeast Asia
edition: Asia countries · Seven regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Asia episode seven of seven. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.

Our final episode is longer, with eleven countries from mainland Southeast Asia into the island world. Singapore uses a labelled supplemental map; Malaysia and Indonesia need special attention because their territory spans separated regions and islands.

states.name: Myanmar
lines: Myanmar lies east of Bangladesh and India, west of Thailand and Laos, and south of China. Its long western and southern shores face the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea.
Bagan spreads temples and stupas across a plain beside the Ayeyarwady River. The landscape records the religious and artistic achievements of an early Buddhist kingdom.
Picture temple silhouettes along a river plain at mainland Southeast Asia’s western edge. Myanmar is west of Thailand, not on the eastern Vietnamese coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Myanmar and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Thailand
lines: Thailand occupies the middle of the mainland group, between Myanmar and Laos, above Cambodia and Malaysia. Its southern arm follows the peninsula toward Malaysia.
Sukhothai was an early capital of Siam. Its monuments show how several cultural influences combined into a distinctive style of Thai art and architecture.
Remember Thailand as a broad northern body with a long southern handle. Place old Sukhothai in the mainland portion, then follow the handle toward Malaysia.

states.name: Laos
lines: Laos is landlocked, east of Thailand and west of Vietnam, with China to the north and Cambodia to the south. It is the inland member of this mainland chain.
The Plain of Jars contains huge stone vessels linked to Iron Age funerary practices. Archaeological evidence connects them with burials, even though many details remain under study.
Picture stone jars inland between Thailand and Vietnam. Rivers cross Laos, but no part of the country reaches the sea.
states.transition: Let's bring Laos and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Cambodia
lines: Cambodia sits below Laos, southeast of Thailand and west of southern Vietnam. Its southwestern edge has a coast on the Gulf of Thailand.
Angkor preserves the remains of successive Khmer capitals, including Angkor Wat and the carved faces at the Bayon. The famous temple belongs to a much larger historical landscape.
Remember Angkor below Laos and inside Vietnam’s coastal curve. Cambodia has a southwestern coast; Laos, immediately north, is landlocked.

states.name: Vietnam
lines: Vietnam follows the eastern coast of the mainland, below China and east of Laos and Cambodia. Its long, narrow central stretch links broader northern and southern regions.
Ha Long Bay and the Cat Ba area contain limestone towers rising from the sea. Water has flooded a karst landscape, leaving a remarkable scattering of rocky islands.
Picture limestone towers beside the long eastern coastal ribbon. Vietnam curves around Laos and Cambodia; Thailand lies farther west.

states.name: Malaysia
lines: Malaysia has two main regions: one on the Malay Peninsula below Thailand, the other on northern Borneo. The South China Sea separates them; both belong to the same country.
Kinabalu Park, in Sabah on Borneo, rises from tropical rainforest into much cooler mountain habitats. A single mountain landscape supports a remarkable range of plant life.
Remember one country in two regions, with Mount Kinabalu on the Borneo side. Singapore sits off the peninsula’s southern tip, while Brunei is tucked into Borneo’s northern coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Malaysia and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Singapore
lines: Singapore is the small island country immediately south of peninsular Malaysia. Indonesia’s nearby islands lie across the strait; this labelled supplemental map shows Singapore separately.
Singapore Botanic Gardens became an important centre of tropical plant research, including work connected with rubber cultivation. A garden helped shape a major regional industry.
Picture a research garden at the peninsula’s southern tip. Singapore is its own country, not a city inside Malaysia, despite the very short crossing between them.
states.transition: Let's find Singapore on a labelled supplemental map, then move in for a closer view.

states.name: Brunei
lines: Brunei is a small country on Borneo’s northern coast, surrounded on land by Malaysia. Malaysian territory separates its two main parts.
Mangroves along the Brunei River are habitat for proboscis monkeys, famous for their large noses. The wildlife hook belongs to Borneo, not the Malay Peninsula.
Picture the long-nosed monkey on Borneo’s north coast. Keep Brunei small and coastal, with Malaysian territory around it and Indonesian Borneo farther south.
states.transition: Let's bring Brunei and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Indonesia
lines: Indonesia stretches across a vast chain of islands between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. It includes Sumatra, Java, much of Borneo, Sulawesi and the western part of New Guinea.
Komodo dragons are giant lizards native to a small part of Indonesia. Their island habitats are protected in Komodo National Park: real reptiles behind a dragon’s name.
Picture the dragon among a long east-west island chain. Borneo is shared with Malaysia and Brunei, and New Guinea is shared with Papua New Guinea; neither whole island is exclusively Indonesian.
states.transition: Let's bring Indonesia and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Philippines
lines: The Philippines is the island country east of Vietnam, north of Indonesia and south of Taiwan. Luzon is toward the north, with Mindanao toward the south.
In the Cordillera mountains, Ifugao rice terraces follow steep slopes in carefully maintained steps. Farming knowledge and water management turned mountainsides into productive fields.
Remember a mostly north-south island group above Indonesia, with rice terraces on northern Luzon. Keep it separate from Indonesia’s much longer east-west chain.
states.transition: Let's bring Philippines and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Timor-Leste
lines: Timor-Leste occupies the eastern part of Timor, plus the separate Oecusse enclave and nearby islands. Indonesia occupies the western part of the main island.
Tais is a handwoven textile used in ceremonies, exchanges and community life. Its colours and patterns carry identities and knowledge passed down by Timorese weavers.
Picture woven cloth at the eastern end of Timor, below Indonesia’s main island chain. The small Oecusse piece also belongs to Timor-Leste, although Indonesian territory surrounds it on land.
states.transition: Let's bring Timor-Leste and its neighbours into view.

recap: On the mainland, Myanmar is west, Thailand central, Laos inland, Cambodia below Laos, and Vietnam along the eastern coast. Malaysia reaches down the peninsula and across to Borneo; Singapore sits off the peninsula’s tip.

Brunei is small and coastal on Borneo. Indonesia stretches east to west, the Philippines forms a more north-south island group above it, and Timor-Leste occupies eastern Timor with its separate enclave.

Across seven episodes, we have visited forty-nine teaching stops. Cyprus counts once, with its separate northern map target explained; Bahrain, Maldives and Singapore use supplemental views. Recall each country through its position and its memorable fact.
